findings.reason: Line 1: the lamed has a qamats, not a patach, and the dalet has no visible dagesh.
End of line 1: the print reads שַׁדּוּן (shin, then dalet with dagesh, then shuruk), as in Job 19:29. It is not שֶׁהוּן. The start of line 2 has בְּדִין with a sheva under the bet, not בַּדִּין.

Line 2: the last letter is a plain resh that sits on the line. Compare the final kaf in אֵיךְ (line 6) and מִתְהַלֵּךְ, which drop below the line and carry an internal mark. This is probably a printer's error for וְהִדְרִיךְ. See uncertainties for the editorial policy question.
Line 3: the print has a holam-vav (הַמּוֹרִים). The candidate left out the vav.

Lines 4–5: line 5 starts with kaf (כ). There is no נִ prefix. The next word is בְּאֵסֶר, with no vav and with segol under the samekh, not בֶּאֱסוֹר. גְּבוּל has a dagesh in the gimel. The pointing of the first kaf needs checking (see uncertainties).
Line 5: there is a sheva under the bet. There is no patach and no dagesh in the shin.
Line 6: the second verb is the niphal יִשָּׁפֵטוּ (qamats under the shin, tsere under the pe, no vav). The candidate wrongly repeated יִשְׁפּוֹטוּ from the line before.
Line 9: the kaf is pointed with a qamats (וְכָל), not a holam.
Line 15: there is a clear sheva under the bet, and no dagesh in the dalet.
Line 18: the print reads תָּמוּט (qamats under the tav, shuruk, no dagesh in the mem).
Line 18: there is a qamats under the kaf, not a patach.
Last line: the print reads שִׂיחִים, with a hiriq-yod before the final mem. It is not שִׂיחָם.
The print clearly reads 'Abibu', a typo for Abihu. A faithful transcription keeps 'Abibu' unless the editorial policy allows correcting it.

uncertainties.question: Should obvious printer's errors be kept as printed or corrected to וְהִדְרִיךְ? The print clearly shows resh.
Same policy question as for וְהִדְרִיר: keep the printed typo or correct it to 'Abihu'?
The vowel under the first kaf (kubutz or sheva) and whether the bet has a dagesh are not certain at this resolution. The consonants כבל are certain.
There is an extra mark next to the tsere under the yod. It could be a meteg, or it could be speckling in the scan.
There is a possible meteg under the yod next to the patach.
Is the vav a shuruk (נוּקַשׁ) or a holam-vav (נוֹקַשׁ)? The dot placement can't be resolved in the band.
The first vowel under the bet looks like it could be a sheva (בְּעֶשֶׂר) rather than a segol. Please confirm at higher magnification.
Is there a dagesh in the bet (בּוֹ)? The second בּוֹ (line 12) does seem to have one.
Is there a dagesh in the pe?
The print may read יְבֻקְּרוּ (sheva under the yod, kubutz under the bet) rather than יִבָּקְרוּ. Please check at higher magnification.
Whether the bet in these words has a dagesh can't be confirmed at band resolution.

coverage_notes: I compared all 30 Hebrew lines of s230 and the full English page of s231 word by word against the full page images and all four bands of s230. I did not open the s231 band images. The s231 English was checked against the full page only, which was legible at that size.
I ignored the running heads and page numbers ('105', 'מוסף ליום ראשון של ראש השנה', 'Musaph for the New Year') as instructed.

Neither page has any bottom text, rubric, condition/alternative instruction, role siglum, Rashi annotation or footnote. Below the last line both pages are blank. I found no source content left out of the candidate.

The English matches the print except for 'Abibu'. 'ma;' in line 2 is a scan artifact for 'may', and the candidate is right to read 'may'. Punctuation and curly quotes match, and the English ends mid-sentence with 'Let them look at', as the page does.
The Hebrew ends with 'שִׂיחִים.' and a period, so the stanza continues on the next page.
